message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1100409 CHARGE_ALREADY_EXISTS (reused reference), 1101422 CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND_FOR_CHARGE, 1102422 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_FOUND_FOR_CHARGE (the payment method must belong to this customer), 1125400 CURRENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED, 1130400 AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM, 1137400 CLIENT_ENCRYPTION_ERROR, 1140400 CHARGE_NOT_SUCCESSFUL, 1141400 REDIRECT_URL_INVALID, 1142400 USSD_BANK_CODE_INVALID, 1150400 INVALID_CHARGE (bank transfer: use /virtual-accounts), 1105500 CHARGE_FAILED, 1119500 FAILED_TO_INITIATE_CHARGE, 1107500 CHARGE_CREATION_FAILED (the table says to retry: reuse the same X-Idempotency-Key).

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: send X-Idempotency-Key on this POST. Docs (Idempotency): "For all `POST` endpoints, include an idempotency key in the request header (`X-Idempotency-Key`)." The API reference marks it optional; the headers guide lists it under 'Mandatory API Headers'. A reused key replays the first response ("the response will include the header `X-Idempotency-Cache-Hit: true`"), so reuse the key when retrying the same operation and use a new one for a new operation. X-Trace-Id is optional. For both: "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters." "Its length should be between 12 and 255 characters." The idempotency page also says "We recommend using a **UUID** string as your idempotency key": strip the UUID's hyphens to satisfy both.

Body: amount (decimal, ≥ 0.01, major units), currency, reference (6-42 chars, ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$, unique), customer_id, payment_method_id; optional redirect_url (needed for redirect flows), recurring, authorization, meta, order_id. A 201 only means the charge was created: decide on data.status and data.next_action, never on the top-level status (the API reference says success / failed; the card guide's sample shows "status": "pending").

data.next_action drives the payment. Docs (General Flow): "For these types of authorization, [update the transaction](/v4.0/reference/charges_put) with the authorization object to complete them." (requires_pin, requires_otp, requires_additional_fields → update_charge). redirect_url → send the customer to next_action.redirect_url.url (an object, not a string; "response.data.next_action.redirect_url.url"). payment_instruction → show next_action.payment_instruction.note (mobile money push, USSD). requires_bank_transfer → show account_number / account_bank_name / account_expiration_datetime. qr_code (mobile_money payment method created with use_qr: true) → next_action.qr_code.image; the API reference's example value is a data:image/png;base64 URI. requires_capture belongs to card pre-authorisation orders, which afrotools does not cover. Treat an unknown type as pending and call get_charge. After each update_charge, read next_action again: "You’ll first need to update the charge with the encrypted card PIN." "Followed by updating the charge request with the OTP."

requires_requery = upstream timeout, not a failure. Docs (Errors): "we return a `requires_requery` with an `HTTP 201 Created` status. This indicates that the charge is being processed and should not be retried." "wait 20 seconds before calling the retrieve [charge](/v4/reference/charges_get)/[order](/v4/reference/orders_get) endpoints"; "If the retrieve request still returns a `requires_requery` response, retry the request in 40 seconds. Transactions that remain unresolved after a minute will transition to a failed status." If you must re-send the POST, reuse the same X-Idempotency-Key.

Method/currency limits: "USSD payments are only available for NGN (Nigerian Naira) collections." OPay: "This payment method is only available for **NGN** (Nigerian Naira) transactions." Pay with Bank (bank_account): "This payment method is only available for NGN (Nigerian Naira) collections." Mobile money: "The charge `currency` must match the `currency_code` used when creating the payment method." The error table gives 1125400 CURRENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED for a mismatch; the mobile money guide's sample returns 10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID ("Currency not supported for GH Mobile Money.").

Fulfil only after verification: Docs (General Flow): "verify the transaction's `reference`, `amount` and `status` before giving value to the customer." The success value of data.status is 'succeeded' (enum: succeeded, pending, failed, voided); also check currency. Pay-with-bank-transfer charges carry a reference generated by Flutterwave, not the virtual account's reference (the guide creates the account with one reference and the incoming charge shows another): match those on the virtual account (list_charges?virtual_account_id=…) or customer_id, plus amount and currency.

Sandbox card scenarios go in X-Scenario-Key as "`scenario:<value>&issuer:<value>`" (auth_pin, auth_pin_3ds, auth_3ds, auth_avs; issuer e.g. approved, insufficient_funds). "If you omit the `X-Scenario-Key` header, all mock card transactions defaults to a `noauth` flow." Mobile money redirect flow: "To simulate the redirect flow, pass `scenario:auth_redirect` in the header."

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1100409 CHARGE_ALREADY_EXISTS (reused reference), 1101422 CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND_FOR_CHARGE, 1102422 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_FOUND_FOR_CHARGE (the payment method must belong to this customer), 1125400 CURRENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED, 1130400 AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM, 1137400 CLIENT_ENCRYPTION_ERROR, 1140400 CHARGE_NOT_SUCCESSFUL, 1141400 REDIRECT_URL_INVALID, 1142400 USSD_BANK_CODE_INVALID, 1150400 INVALID_CHARGE (bank transfer: use /virtual-accounts), 1105500 CHARGE_FAILED, 1119500 FAILED_TO_INITIATE_CHARGE, 1107500 CHARGE_CREATION_FAILED (the table says to retry: reuse the same X-Idempotency-Key). Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
